title-group.article-title: Paired-biopsy analysis of PSMA expression before and after androgen-receptor pathway inhibition in metastatic prostate cancer.

contrib-group.aff: Eastgate Cancer Research Network, New York, NY
Southern Clinical Oncology Center, Atlanta, GA
Pacific Precision Medicine Institute, San Francisco, CA

abstract.p: Background: Acquired resistance to androgen-receptor pathway inhibition in metastatic castration-resistant prostate cancer may involve dynamic changes in therapeutic targets and associated signaling pathways. We evaluated longitudinal changes in PSMA using paired tumor samples collected before treatment and at disease progression. Methods: Institutional databases were queried to identify patients with metastatic castration-resistant prostate cancer who received androgen-receptor pathway inhibition and had paired pretreatment and post-progression biopsies. Samples were assessed by quantitative immunohistochemistry and spatial transcriptomics. Marker abundance was compared within patients, and associations with clinical outcomes were explored using nonparametric tests. Results: Paired samples from 27 patients passed quality control. Median progression-free survival on therapy was 6.6 months. Baseline PSMA expression was 185 H-score, with a median on-treatment change of −19%. Substantial loss of PSMA was observed in 10 patients, whereas the remaining samples showed stable or increased expression. Neuroendocrine marker expression changed by +31% across paired samples (p=0.06). The aggregate pattern was consistent with phenotypic diversification with partial loss of target expression. Conclusions: Longitudinal changes in PSMA after androgen-receptor pathway inhibition were heterogeneous in metastatic castration-resistant prostate cancer. Resistance was not explained by a single uniform biomarker shift, supporting multi-analyte assessment of paired samples and further mechanistic study. Research Sponsor: None.
